title: Canonical acyclic Cech edges commute with additive maps, site change, and forgetting module structure
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites with final objects and abelian sheaf cohomology [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $\mathcal U=(U_i\to1_{\mathcal C})$ be a finite covering, $A$ an abelian sheaf, and assume $H^r(U_{i_0}\times\cdots\times U_{i_t},A)=0$ for every $r>0$ and every nonempty tuple. The canonical edge map $e_{\mathcal U,A}^q:\check H^q(\mathcal U,A)\to H^q(\mathcal C,A)$ [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] is an isomorphism for $q\ge0$. Its normalization is $H^q(\alpha)^{-1}H^q(\beta)$, where, for an injective resolution $A\to I^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], $\alpha$ is restriction from $\Gamma(I^\bullet)$ to $\operatorname{Tot}(\check C^\bullet(\mathcal U,I^\bullet))$, with total differential $d_C+(-1)^t d_I$ in Cech degree $t$ [def-sp-double-complex-total] and $\beta$ is induced by the resolution augmentation. These maps are independent of the resolution and natural for every morphism of abelian sheaves between objects satisfying the stated acyclicity, without any linearity assumption.
Let $f:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be a morphism of sites presented by a continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserving the final object and the tuple fibre products of $\mathcal U$, and carrying $\mathcal U$ to a covering $u\mathcal U$. Let $B$ be an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal D$, acyclic on every tuple intersection of $u\mathcal U$, and let $h:A\to f_*B$ be an additive sheaf map. Its section components define $h_C:\check C(\mathcal U,A)\to\check C(u\mathcal U,B)$. If $h_H:H^q(\mathcal C,A)\to H^q(\mathcal D,B)$ is the canonical cohomology map of $h$ (equivalently, inverse-image pullback followed by the adjoint $f^{-1}A\to B$), then $h_H e_{\mathcal U,A}^q=e_{u\mathcal U,B}^q H^q(h_C)$.
Finally, module cohomology means the right derived functors of evaluation in sheaves of modules, computed by injective resolutions [def-sp-left-exact-additive, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of rings on $\mathcal C$, and $M$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] acyclic on the tuple intersections in both module and underlying abelian cohomology. After identifying the underlying section Cech complexes, its canonical module Cech edge followed by the canonical module-to-abelian cohomology identification equals $e_{\mathcal U,M_{ab}}^q$. Here $M_{ab}$ is $M$ with scalar multiplication forgotten; the canonical identification is the unique morphism of universal $\delta$-functors inducing the identity on degree-zero sections [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor].

The site-change and forgetting squares assert compatibility of these specified augmentations.

proof.text: Choose a nonnegative injective resolution $a:A\to I^\bullet$ in abelian sheaves. Put $D^{t,r}=\prod_{\mathbf i\in I_{\mathcal U}^{t+1}}I^r(U_{\mathbf i})$, where $I_{\mathcal U}$ denotes the finite index set of the covering (not the resolution). The Cech restriction differential commutes with the resolution differential by naturality. Define $\alpha^n$ by restricting $I^n(1)$ to the $(0,n)$ summand of $T=\operatorname{Tot}D$, and $\beta^n$ by applying $a$ on every component of $\check C^n(\mathcal U,A)$ and including the $(n,0)$ summand. Both are chain maps: restrictions of a global section have zero Cech differential, $d_Ia=0$, and the vertical sign is $+1$ on the image of $\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 03AX, lemma-cech-cohomology, construction of alpha and beta

proof.text: For each $r$, the augmented row $0\to I^r(1)\to\check C^0(\mathcal U,I^r)\to\check C^1(\mathcal U,I^r)\to\cdots$ is exact: its positive cohomology vanishes by injective Cech acyclicity, and its degree-zero kernel is precisely the image of restriction by the sheaf equalizer condition. Apply the first-quadrant augmentation lemma with the first index the Cech degree. Its augmentation is $\alpha$, so $\alpha$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Each diagonal has only $n+1$ summands; no boundedness of the Cech degree is needed.

source.place: Tag 0133, lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution, second-variable variant; applied as in sites-cohomology Tag 03AX

proof.text: For each fixed $t$, the resolution column has cohomology $\prod_{\mathbf i}H^r(U_{\mathbf i},A)$: kernels and images of the differential in a finite product are computed componentwise. The augmentation identifies its degree-zero kernel with $\prod_{\mathbf i}A(U_{\mathbf i})$, and the hypothesis makes all positive cohomology zero. Apply the same augmentation lemma with the resolution index first to obtain that $\beta$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Explicitly the transposed total has differential $d_I+(-1)^r d_C$; multiplication by $(-1)^{tr}$ on bidegree $(t,r)$ identifies it with $T$, and is the identity on $r=0$, so its augmentation becomes exactly $\beta$. Thus the specified edge $H^q(\alpha)^{-1}H^q(\beta)$ is an isomorphism for every $q\ge0$.

source.place: Tag 03F7, lemma-cech-spectral-sequence-application, acyclicity; Tag 03AX augmentation model, with Homology Tag 0133

proof.text: For an additive coefficient map $g:A\to A'$, lift $g$ to a map $v:I^\bullet\to I'^\bullet$ of injective resolutions. On bidegree $(t,r)$ apply $v^r$ to each section. This defines a total map $V:T\to T'$ and gives the literal chain-map equations $V\alpha=\alpha'\Gamma(v)$ and $V\beta=\beta'\check C(g)$. On cohomology, $H(\Gamma(v))$ is the canonical coefficient map. Multiplying the first equation by the inverses of $H(\alpha)$ and $H(\alpha')$ and using the second proves $H(g)e_A=e_{A'}H(\check C(g))$. This uses only additivity and commutation with restrictions, so semilinear maps that are additive are allowed.

source.place: Tag 03AX, omitted verification of functoriality, supplied explicitly; Derived Categories Tag 013P

proof.text: Take $g=\mathrm{id}_A$ in the preceding step to compare any two resolutions. Any two lifts are homotopic, by applying uniqueness of lifts to the quasi-isomorphism $A[0]\to I^\bullet$. If $v-w=d k+k d$, the induced total maps are homotopic via $K|_{(t,r)}=(-1)^t\check C^t(k^r)$. Indeed the two horizontal contributions cancel, while the two vertical contributions are $d_Ik+kd_I$ because the two signs $(-1)^t$ multiply to $1$. On global sections the homotopy is $\Gamma(k)$. Therefore all induced cohomology maps agree. Comparisons for identities and compositions agree by the same uniqueness, giving resolution independence of the specified edge under the canonical cohomology identifications.

source.place: Tag 013S, lemma-morphisms-equal-up-to-homotopy; applied to Tag 03AX augmentations

proof.text: For site change choose $B\to J^\bullet$ injective on $\mathcal D$. Exactness of $f^{-1}$ makes $f^{-1}A[0]\to f^{-1}I^\bullet$ a degreewise monomorphic quasi-isomorphism. Lift the map $f^{-1}A[0]\to B[0]\to J^\bullet$, whose first arrow is adjoint to $h$, along this augmentation to $j:f^{-1}I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$, strictly over the augmentations. Adjunction gives $v:I^\bullet\to f_*J^\bullet$. Its section maps are $I^r(V)\to J^r(uV)$, compatible with every restriction. Their global map $w:\Gamma_{\mathcal C}I\to\Gamma_{\mathcal D}J$ computes $h_H$. To check the last assertion against the canonical pullback, insert an injective resolution $L$ of $f^{-1}A$, a lift $f^{-1}I\to L$, and a coefficient lift $L\to J$; the canonical pullback and coefficient formulas compute their composite on sections. Its composite is homotopic to $j$ by lift uniqueness, so it has the same cohomology map.

source.place: Tag 013P, lemma-morphisms-lift, part (2); sites-cohomology Tag 03AX augmentations and canonical site pullback

proof.text: The section components of $v$ define $V^{t,r}:\check C^t(\mathcal U,I^r)\to\check C^t(u\mathcal U,J^r)$, using the canonical tuple-product identifications preserved by $u$. For each omitted index $a$, the equation $v_{U_{\mathbf i}}\operatorname{res}_a=\operatorname{res}_{u(a)}v_{U_{\mathbf i\setminus a}}$ shows that $V$ commutes with $d_C$; since $v$ is a chain map it commutes with $d_I$ and hence the total differential. On the two axes the equations are $V\alpha_{\mathcal C}=\alpha_{\mathcal D}w$ and $V\beta_A=\beta_B h_C$. Both are literal equalities: the former is restriction naturality, the latter is the strictly commuting lifted augmentation of step 6. Applying cohomology and inverting both $H(\alpha)$ proves $h_H e_{\mathcal U,A}=e_{u\mathcal U,B}H(h_C)$. The two edges are isomorphisms by steps 2--3 using the separately assumed acyclicity of $A$ and $B$.

source.place: Tag 03AX, its two specified augmentations; agent verification of the site-change square

proof.text: The category of sheaves of left $\mathcal O$-modules on the small site $\mathcal C$ is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], in a universe containing the site and coefficient values. Hence it has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. For modules choose a nonnegative injective module resolution $M\to P^\bullet$, as in the statement's convention for module cohomology. After forgetting scalars it remains an exact augmented resolution: kernels are sectionwise and the underlying sheaf of a cokernel is the sheafification of the sectionwise abelian cokernel, so forgetting preserves kernels and cokernels. Every $P^r_{ab}$ is acyclic for abelian evaluation at every object by the ringed-site injective-module acyclicity theorem; it is not asserted to be an injective abelian sheaf. The acyclic-resolution theorem therefore identifies $H^q(\Gamma(P_{ab}))$ with $H^q(\mathcal C,M_{ab})$, by any augmentation-preserving map $P_{ab}\to J$ to an abelian injective resolution. Such a strict map exists by the monomorphic quasi-isomorphism lifting lemma. Denote it by $k$.

source.place: Tag 03FD, lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree, proof, acyclicity of injective modules; Derived Categories acyclic-resolution criterion; injectives.tex Tag 079Q (remark-existence-D), final sentence, and Tag 079H (theorem-injective-embedding-grothendieck), for existence of the module resolution

proof.text: The canonical module-to-abelian identification is the resolution map $H^q(\Gamma(k))$ just obtained. Here is its normalization: the module right-derived delta-functor is universal, while abelian cohomology precomposed with exact forgetting is a delta-functor and vanishes in positive degrees on module injectives. Hence it is effaceable and universal as well, and the unique delta-functor morphism inducing the identity on sections is an isomorphism. Its value on $M\to P^\bullet$ is the acyclic-resolution comparison: successively put $M_0=M$, $M_{r+1}=\operatorname{coker}(M_r\to P^r)$ and use $0\to M_r\to P^r\to M_{r+1}\to0$. In degree one both comparisons are induced by the identity on sections modulo the image of $\Gamma(P^0)$; in higher degrees the connecting isomorphisms reduce degree by one, since the positive cohomology of each $P^r$ vanishes in both theories. Induction therefore identifies the universal comparison with $H^q(\Gamma(k))$ in every degree, with the same connecting-map convention.

source.place: Tag 03FD, lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree, first paragraph; Derived Categories Tag 015B and Homology Tag 010T

proof.text: For $P$ the module restriction augmentation $\alpha_P:\Gamma(P)\to\operatorname{Tot}\check C(\mathcal U,P)$ is a quasi-isomorphism by injective-module Cech acyclicity, the degree-zero sheaf equalizer, and the same augmentation lemma used in step 2. The module coefficient augmentation $\beta_M$ is a quasi-isomorphism by step 3 applied to module evaluation and the assumed module acyclicity on every tuple. Underlying section Cech complexes and both axis maps are unchanged on forgetting scalars. Applying $\check C$ termwise to $k:P_{ab}\to J$ gives $K$ between the two totals with $K\alpha_P=\alpha_J\Gamma(k)$ and $K\beta_M=\beta_{M_{ab}}$, component by component. Consequently $H(\Gamma(k))H(\alpha_P)^{-1}H(\beta_M)=H(\alpha_J)^{-1}H(\beta_{M_{ab}})$, the required compatibility with the canonical identification of step 9. No claim that forgetting preserves injectives or that tensoring with the ring sheaf is exact occurs.
